newsitem.title: USA: U.S. BLS's Abraham says CPI revision on track.
newsitem.headline: U.S. BLS's Abraham says CPI revision on track.

text.p: Katharine Abraham, Commissioner of the U.S. Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), said her Department is on schedule for the introduction of a revised retail inflation gauge at the start of 1997.

"We are on schedule with the revision of the (Consumer Price Index)," Abraham told the National Association of Business Economists here. "In January 1997, we will introduce a new market basket (in the CPI)."
Among the revisions, Abraham said the BLS is changing the way it handles medical care.
"The formula bias problem has been corrected in the July CPI," Abraham added, referring to the way products are introduced in the calculation of the CPI.
The Commissioner said her Department has been affected by sizable budget cuts. To overcome the cuts, she said the Department is setting priorities and increasing efficiencies.
But beyond budget cuts, Abraham said she had two concerns that were even more prominent in her mind.

"I am greatly concerned over the fact many employers fail to respond to the parts of the surveys that are mandatory," said said. "They are not persuaded by the value of these statistical data to their own operations."
In addition, Abraham said she is concered about the "politicization" of data.

"I hear people say they believe the data in some way have become politicized. Commenting on the 250,000 payrolls in August, I hear on television programs (that) the Clinton Administration needed a good number and, of course, they got it. These are totally irresponsible and totally unfounded allegations."
The 250,000 new payrolls added last month brought the total number of jobs created during the Clinton years to some 10.5 million.
